These test-only reference records were captured from the public Wikipedia and Wikidata APIs on 2026-10-11 for Hamburg, Tokyo, Manila, and Adamstown. Production code does not import them.

The JSON retains article titles, coordinates, Wikidata identifiers, and the labels, descriptions, relationship qualifiers, addresses and opening references needed to reproduce destination verification. Historical administrative claims remain in the fixtures to prevent the country-mismatch regression. The first three catalogs are limited to 24 verified places to keep the fixture small; Adamstown retains its returned pages even though none passes the required destination/place checks. Photos are deliberately unavailable in these adapter fixtures.

Sources: `https://en.wikipedia.org/w/api.php` (coordinate/page-property query) and `https://www.wikidata.org/w/api.php` (entity query). Each entity's source is `https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/<entity ID>`. Wikidata structured data is CC0; Wikipedia titles and coordinates are reference metadata, with no article text included.

Run `node --test --experimental-strip-types tests/multi-destination-generation.test.ts` for offline regression coverage. To verify actual PostgreSQL persistence in a newly created temporary schema, from the backend directory run `scripts/verify-shared-generation.ts` with `TRAVELMATE_ALLOW_ISOLATED_SCHEMA=1`. It uses the configured database's direct endpoint for schema isolation, applies existing migrations only in that new schema, invokes shared generation/save/reopen handlers, exports browser fixtures, and removes only that schema. No existing trips or application connection settings are changed. Credentials stay in the server environment and are never printed.
